With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. Consistent with the literature on forward guidance and quantitative easing, keeping the policy rate near zero while tapering asset purchases is intended to preserve accommodative financial conditions and anchor expectations around the 2 percent inflation target. The move toward normalization aligns with Taylor-rule principles highlighted in academic work (e.g., Clarida and others) in the aftermath of a pandemic-driven supply shock, implying a cautiously optimistic outlook balanced by elevated inflation and virus-related risks.
